label: Mycenaean
description: Palace culture; earliest evidence of some deities (Linear B tablets name a 'Po-ti-ni-a,' possibly Athena or a mother-goddess, and a 'Di-wi-je-u,' possibly Zeus).

label: Hesiod & Homer
description: The Iliad, Odyssey, and the Theogony are composed (orated/written). The Olympian pantheon takes its classical literary shape.

label: Archaic
description: Great sanctuaries flourish: Olympia, Delphi, Dodona. Vase painting depicts the myths. The Homeric Hymns are composed.

label: Classical
description: The classical pantheon is fixed; the Parthenon is built for Athena (447–432 BCE). Tragedy and comedy flourish at the Dionysia.

label: Hellenistic
description: Apollo becomes strongly identified with the sun; mystery cults and syncretism (e.g. Sarapis) spread. Later myths (e.g. Ovid's) are composed.

label: Roman & Later
description: Greek gods are equated with Roman ones (Zeus=Jupiter, etc.). Pausanias writes his survey of Greek sanctuaries (c. 150–180 CE).
